_header: Parity fixture for crates/daemon/src/characters.rs ->
daemon/src/characters.ts.
Generated by driving the real Rust CharacterRegistry in a throwaway
worktree at 9023b46d (the last commit where the daemon crate builds).
The generator is not committed; nothing regenerates this file. A later
diff against it is a defect, not a fixture to update.
characters.rs is byte-identical between 9023b46d and the commit this
ports at, so the worktree's answers are HEAD's answers. The four
config/mod.rs functions it calls — discover_characters,
load_character_definition, resolve_user_definition and
resolve_prompt_template — are unchanged there too; everything that did
change in that file since 9023b46d was the dreaming removal.
EVERY CASE IS A SCRIPTED RUN, not a single call. Every decision in this
module is about caching — whether the second call sees the first one's
work — and none of them is visible from one call. `available` is a
cached scan that only `refresh` and `reload_runtime_state` update;
engines are cached until a reload drops them, and a `refresh` alone
does not; per-character config caches its own ABSENCE, so writing the
override file after the first lookup changes nothing until something
invalidates.
`state.snapshots` is read off disk, not from the registry: it lists the
characters with an `active_prompt/` directory. The registry calls
ensure_active_prompt_snapshot for every discovered character on
construction, on refresh and on reload, and only then. Which of the
three do it is this module's decision and is invisible elsewhere.
`effective_config` records three marks rather than a whole config.
`display_name` and `addr` are set ONLY in the global file, so a merge
that ran against the real global table can be told from one that ran
against an empty base. That distinction is real and load-bearing: the
registry merges a character override over `global_config.raw_table()`,
which is None for a config built with `LoadedConfig::new_for_test` —
the shape the Rust's own unit tests use. Under that shape a character
override loses every global setting. Production builds the registry
from `load_config`, which populates the raw table. Both are recorded;
the Rust's unit tests only ever exercise the second.
Engine identity is recorded as a small integer assigned in first-seen
order, from Arc::as_ptr. It is what pins 'the cached engine came back'
and 'the dropped engine did not'; an address would have made the
fixture machine-specific for no gain.
